help:
**Commands.** Write one per line, starting with `/harness` or `@jgoetzmann-bot`; the two work the same way.

| Verb | What it does | Where | Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| `build [notes]` | queue this issue for the bot | issue | 2 |
| `fullsend [notes]` | split this issue into parts that land on one branch, then reconcile them into one pull request | issue | 2 |
| `revise <notes>` | queue a revision of this PR with your notes | pull request | 2 |
| `review [strong\|medium] [notes]` | queue a review run of this PR's head, by that tier or stronger; no revision | pull request | 2 |
| `rebuild` | close my PR and build its issue again from `main`, its branch kept | issue or PR | 2 |
| `stop` | take this issue or PR out of the queue and stop work on it | issue or PR | 2 |
| `suggest` | ask for improvement suggestions the next time a lane has nothing to start | anywhere | 2 |
| `approve`, `reject` | alone on a line, no prefix needed: build one of my suggestions, or close it unbuilt | suggestion | 2 |
| `status` | halt state, each subscription, the queue | anywhere | 1 |
| `help [verb]` | this list, or one command in detail | anywhere | 1 |
| `halt [reason]` | stop all model work until `start` | anywhere | 3 |
| `start [subscription]` | lift a halt; with a subscription, lift its suspension instead | anywhere | 3 |
| `run [#n]` | start a run now, outside a subscription's hours if need be | anywhere | 3 |
| `suspend <subscription> [reason]` | start no new work on one subscription until `resume <subscription>` | anywhere | 3 |

Anything else after `/harness` or `@jgoetzmann-bot` is a request: a build on an issue, a revision on a PR, with your words as the notes. A single word that looks like a misspelt verb (`stauts`) runs nothing; I ask what you meant.
After `@jgoetzmann-bot`, a control verb followed by more words reads as plain English, so `@jgoetzmann-bot stop using the old sprite` is a request. Write the verb alone, or with a colon (`@jgoetzmann-bot halt: away this week`), for the command.
Add `--force` (level 3) to `build`, `fullsend`, `revise` or `suggest` to start now, outside a subscription's hours if need be. Label an issue `difficulty:easy`, `difficulty:medium` (the default) or `difficulty:hard` to set the weakest model tier that may build it; `difficulty:hard` keeps it for Opus.
Labels do the same as the verbs: `bot:build` on an issue, `bot:revise` on a PR; assigning @jgoetzmann-bot queues the thread.
An issue is mine (my `bot:…` labels) or people's, never both: `human` keeps me off it, and `human required` is my hand-over when I find I cannot do it (I take my labels off, unassign myself, assign you and say what a person must do). Take either label off to hand it back, then `/harness build`.
On your comment: 👀 seen · 👍 a model will read it · 🚀 answered · ❤️ a run has it · 🎉 done · 😕 it ended without an answer.

fullsend

**`fullsend [notes]`** (level 2, maintainer)

Split this issue into parts, sub-issues that each own their files (or take the sub-issues it has already as its parts), and build each onto one branch of this issue's own, not `main`, with no pull request, checks or review of its own. When the last part closes, one run reconciles the branch with fullsend, makes every check green and opens one pull request into `main`, reviewed like any build.

For example: `/harness fullsend`. `/harness help` (or `@jgoetzmann-bot help`) lists the commands.
review

**`review [strong|medium] [notes]`** (level 2, maintainer)

Queue a review run of the head of one of my pull requests, and no revision: the head stays as it is. With `strong` or `medium` the review waits for a model of that tier or stronger rather than taking a weaker one. Your notes reach the reviewer.

For example: `/harness review strong check the replay`. `/harness help` (or `@jgoetzmann-bot help`) lists the commands.
suggest

**`suggest`** (level 2, maintainer; also written `suggestions`)

Ask for a suggestion survey the next time a lane has nothing to start, without waiting out the 30 idle minutes a survey otherwise waits for.

For example: `@jgoetzmann-bot suggest`. `/harness help` (or `@jgoetzmann-bot help`) lists the commands.

halt

**`halt [reason]`** (level 3, operator)

Stop all model work until `start`; a run already going stops at its next checkpoint. After `@jgoetzmann-bot`, a colon after the verb gives the reason.

For example: `@jgoetzmann-bot halt: away this week`. `/harness help` (or `@jgoetzmann-bot help`) lists the commands.
start

**`start [subscription]`** (level 3, operator; also written `resume`, `unhalt`)

Lift a halt. `start --force` also starts a run now. With a subscription (`resume claude-3`), lift that one's suspension and leave a halt as it is.

For example: `/harness start --force`. `/harness help` (or `@jgoetzmann-bot help`) lists the commands.
resume

**`start [subscription]`** (level 3, operator; also written `resume`, `unhalt`)

Lift a halt. `start --force` also starts a run now. With a subscription (`resume claude-3`), lift that one's suspension and leave a halt as it is.

For example: `/harness start --force`. `/harness help` (or `@jgoetzmann-bot help`) lists the commands.
run

**`run [#n]`** (level 3, operator; also written `go`)

Start a run now, outside a subscription's hours if need be, for one item or whatever is next in the queue.

For example: `@jgoetzmann-bot run #12`. `/harness help` (or `@jgoetzmann-bot help`) lists the commands.
suspend

**`suspend <subscription> [reason]`** (level 3, operator)

Start no new work on one subscription (an id `status` lists, such as `claude-3` or `gpt`) until `/harness resume <subscription>`; a run already going on it stops at its next checkpoint, keeps its work and goes back to the queue for another subscription. `--force` does not lift it. After `@jgoetzmann-bot`, a colon after the verb gives the reason.

For example: `@jgoetzmann-bot suspend: claude-3 using it myself`. `/harness help` (or `@jgoetzmann-bot help`) lists the commands.
status

**`status`** (level 1, asker)

Halt state, which subscriptions are running what right now, each subscription (its hours, usage, and what it is doing), and what is queued.

For example: `@jgoetzmann-bot status`. `/harness help` (or `@jgoetzmann-bot help`) lists the commands.
help

**`help [verb]`** (level 1, asker)

The list of commands, or one of them in detail.

For example: `/harness help build`. `/harness help` (or `@jgoetzmann-bot help`) lists the commands.
stop

**`stop`** (level 2, maintainer)

Take this issue or pull request out of the queue. A run working on it gives up at its next checkpoint and keeps what it has.

For example: `/harness stop`. `/harness help` (or `@jgoetzmann-bot help`) lists the commands.
rebuild

**`rebuild`** (level 2, maintainer)

Close my pull request for this issue, keep its branch as `bot/old/issue-<n>-<date>`, and queue the issue to build again from `main`, at the same difficulty. The new build is told what went wrong with the old one.

For example: `/harness rebuild`. `/harness help` (or `@jgoetzmann-bot help`) lists the commands.
